              1            I, John Welsome, do say and declare as follows
              2             1. I am the owner of Plaintiff Credilogical Systems LLC (formerly known as ACA
              3 Receivables CO., LLC) ("PlaintifF'). If called as a witness, I would competently testify to all of the
              4 following facts which are within my personal knowledge. I make this declaration in support of
              s Plaintiff's opposition to the claim of exemption filed by defendant Carolyn Evans.
              6            2. I have been in the collections business for more than twenty years. Specifically, I
              7 am the owner and manager ofCredilogical Systems LLC. During the time period in question here,
              8 I was the manager of ACA Receivables Co, LLC. I was responsible for overseeing all collection
              9 activities at the time and responsible for overseeing and implementing all processes with respect to
            10 collections activity. At all relevant times, I have had access to all documents relating to the
            11 collection activity on accounts, including those documents pertainmg to Carolyn Evans. It is and
            12 always has been standard business practices to document all activity pertaining to a collection
            13 accoimt, mcluding the account relating to Carolyn Evans. I attest that these documents are securely
            14 stored and maintained and updated in the ordinary course of business at or near the time of the
            IS transactions.
            16             3. The debt at issue here relates to an unpaid bill fi-om Pacific Bell's telephone services
            17 rendered, which final bill was issued on November 18, 2002. On or about November 19, 2004,
            18 Pacific Bell assigned the unpaid debt to Plaintiff. Attached hereto as Exhibit A is PlaintifFs
            19 collection notes pertaining to the debt at issue with Carolyn Evans. Pacific Bell assigned the account
            20 relating to an unpaid debt by Carolyn Evans, with Driver's License # B4977878 and Social Security
            21 No. 549-49-2920. See Ex. A. Pacific Bell would assign unpaid debts to Plaintiff based upon the
            22 information used to open account with Pacific Bell.
            23             4. On December 27, 2005, Plaintiff filed a lawsuit in the superior court of San
            24 Francisco. A tme and correct copy of the conformed copy of the complaint is attached hereto as
            2S Exhibit B.
            26             5. On January 31 , 2006 at 12:23 p.m., Ms. Evans was personally served by a registered
            27 process server with the summons and complaint at her place of employment located at 897 Hinckley

              2 Exhibit C. Judgment was obtained against Ms. Evans on April 10, 2006. A true and correct copy
              3 of the judgment is attached hereto as Exhibit D.
              4            6. Ms. Evans claim that there was a mistake in identity has no merit. As reflected in
              3 the collection notes attached as Exhibit A, Plaintiff had many conversations with Ms. Evans over
              6 the course of many years—before and after judgment was obtained. As manager of Plaintiff at the
              7 time, I can attest that each time Plaintiff calls or receives a call from a debtor. Plaintiff asked
              8 verification information (i.e. name, address, social, etc) from the debtor to ensure that it is the debtor
              9 we are speaking to. This practice is customary today and has been the standard practice of Plaintiff
             10 for decades. Each and every time communication was made with Ms. Evans, she would have had
             11 to identify herself using these unique verifications. Moreover, Ms. Evans claim that there was a
             12 mistake identity is nonsensical because she would not have offered to come up with payment
             13 solutions. Ms. Evans claim would have this Court believe that a person stole her identity to open
             14 up an account with Pacific BeU and then spend years talking to a collection agency trying to pay off
             13 the bill. That makes no sense at all—if someone fraudulently opened an account, the fi-audster
             16 would not offer to pay it off. Moreover, if the account was really fraudulent, then Carolyn Evans
             17 would not have offered to pay off the account from 2005 - 2008. Hence, Carolyn Evans claim that
            18 there is a mistake in identify has no merit.
            19             7. According to the collection notes, Ms. Evans called Plaintiff on numerous occasions
            20 and tried to make payments on the account. At no time did Ms. Evans ever claim that the account
             21 was fraudulent. The only time she did claim that the account was opened up fraudulently was on
            22 December 24, 2008. However, that claim was not supported by any evidence and came years after
            23 the judgment was obtained against her and after having speaking with her to pay off the debt.
            24             8. Indeed, the telephone number that Plaintiff used to communicate with Ms. Evans and
            25 the number that she called in from was 415-424-7900. This is reflected on the collection notes on
            26 the last page as sometime in or around 2010, Ms. Evans changed her number.

              2 various credit sources on individuals. The People Map search report reveals that the telephone

              3 number of 415-424-7900 belonged to Ms. Evans. This report is attached hereto as Exhibit E.
              4             10. Finally, the evidence that Ms. Evans has submitted in support of her claim of
              5 exemption is not persuasive. She submitted an email which claims she was not living at the address
              6 where the debt was incurred based solely on her recollection. She offers no evidence whatsoever.
              7 Nor could she credibly do so because in light of the foregoing, the judgment at issue here pertains
              8 to the debt incurred by Ms. Evans. The evidence that Ms. Evans has submitted is attached hereto as
              9 ExhibitF.
